title: Term deposits options
body:
O.P.
My 30 yr daughter has received an inheritance of $170,000. She is planning on taking out $20,000 but is not sure what to do with the balance. She wants to "park" it away for 12 months whilst she thinks about what to do. The 1yr-18 months term deposits are paying returns of 0.25-0.30%. Are there any better safe financial options ?

---- replies ----
[User #8130712996 postsandrew99999PassiveInvestingAustralia.comWhirlpool Forums Addict] Yea, HISA rates are the best you will get for a risk-free investment.
And if it may be needed within a year or two, the risk of short term loss (which then becomes permanent when it is redeemed) is not worth it for an extra couple of percent.
The limitations of being needed in the short term come with a low very return if you don't want the chance of losing a chunk of it.
[User #10400215530 postscluster2Whirlpool Forums Addict] ING offers 1.35% with no fees, the money is available at any time and it's a bank so 100% safe.
[User #77387420440 postsGazz 333Whirlpool Forums Addict] karpat writes...
The 1yr-18 months term deposits are paying returns of 0.25-0.30%. Are there any better safe financial options ?
If you or any of her siblings have a mortgage with an offset drop it in that. It's accessible if she needs it and whoever has the mortgage can return her something higher (2-3% more likely).
[User #2940236908 posts096igbWhirlpool Forums Addict] What is the most important thing regarding the money to your daughter? being unable to withdraw or getting a slightly better interest rate.
Because your thread title indicates term deposits, I suggest not being able to withdraw without penalty is more important.
Suggest that you look around for rates closer to 1% pa rather than the 0.25% pa that you have seen so far. All banks have a government guarantee up to $250,000.
[User #118463548 postssharianWhirlpool Enthusiast] Do you have a mortgage offset. I have let the kids park money in there in the past and paid them the interest I saved.
[User #8854642972 postsRob10Whirlpool Forums Addict] Term deposits are on the nose.
Other have mentioned savings accounts that a at call with better interest rates. These have less restrictions, what happens is your daughter finds a home or xxxxxxxx she wants in 9 months. There are costs getting money out of term deposits early – the costs are in the banks favour.
Try to encourage your daughter to hurry up working out where the money is to be used. Bank interest then paying tax on that is not a good investment option.
[User #79193913022 postsgregbluesWhirlpool Forums Addict] Term deposits are paying as little as 0.25%.
McQuarrie bank and Rabo are paying about 0.90% on accounts with minimal or no conditions. The former might even be paying a bonus rate for the first 3 or 4 months.
Always check what conditions the banks are enforcing when opening a savings account.
[User #237231315 postskarpatForum Regular] O.P.
096igb writes...
What is the most important thing regarding the money to your daughter? being unable to withdraw or getting a slightly better interest rate.
This is a important consideration. She is aware that she might be tempted to fritter it away or impulsively spend. Wants to avoid making poor decisions and to give herself a year to carefully think about what to do.
[User #47060918541 postsDeedee MegadoodooRetired & living my best life!Whirlpool Forums Addict] I’ve moved a lot of funds to NZ, current TD’s for 12 months are 2.3% for 12 months to 3% for 3 years. I’ve got some TD’s that I fixed for 5 years back in 2019 at 3.8%. That works for me as it’s one way, I don’t intend to bring the funds back to Aus.
NZ has good rates for term deposits but really low rates for on-call whereas in Aus, on-call isn’t too bad but term deposits are atrocious.
[User #79193913022 postsgregbluesWhirlpool Forums Addict] Deedee Megadoodoo writes...
NZ has good rates for term deposits but really low rates for on-call whereas in Aus, on-call isn’t too bad but term deposits are atrocious.
Unless you are a NZ citizen you can't put any money in a NZ term deposit even if you are a customer with ANZ.
[User #584453415 postsMLRForum Regular] > McQuarrie bank and Rabo are paying about 0.90% on accounts with minimal or no conditions.
I ended up closing out my SMSF term deposits I had with rabobank. Their KYC (Know Your Client) demands became intrusive & obsessive. fyi ...
[User #133368219 postssoldatForum Regular] karpat writes...
1yr-18 months term deposits are paying returns of 0.25-0.30%. Are there any better safe financial options ?
AMP bank 1 year TD is 1% for amounts above $25k and 1.35% for 18 months, probably not the right time to lock it in for that long.
[User #593893498 postsSpeedDemon12Forum Regular] cluster2 writes...
ING offers 1.35% with no fees, the money is available at any time and it's a bank so 100% safe.
ING Savings Maximiser is not recommended. There are too many hoops to jump through in order to get the 1.35%. I'd suggest AMP Bank Saver account, easier to qualify for the bonus interest.
[User #2781436058 postsTerran ForeverGreat minds discuss ideasWhirlpool Forums Addict] I was just looking around today and AMP seem to have a really good deal considering what most are offering. A 5 year term deposit is decent at 3.1% interest. Sure it's a long period but a decent way to park a bit of money safely if you are not going to need it for that time. 4 years is 3% I think and down with each shorter term.
[User #47060918541 postsDeedee MegadoodooRetired & living my best life!Whirlpool Forums Addict] mdw000 writes...
AMP is now 3.55% for a 5 year TD.
That's excellent, but with several rate rises possibly on the horizon, locking it in for 5 years I'm not sure if I'd do that. My 5 year TD's that I entered into in 2019 are at 3.8%, they're still serving me well. I've a couple of other TD's at 3% that are ending at Xmas, I think that might be an ideal time to fix a multi year rate then, I'm hoping for an interest rate of at least 4.5% fingers crossed!
